title: Apartment-society maintenance dues
summary: A small web app for a residents' association treasurer: a dues ledger per flat, reminder messages drafted but never sent, and a numbered receipt for every payment.
context: Greenfold Terraces is a fictional 80-flat apartment society. Its volunteer treasurer tracks monthly maintenance in a spreadsheet, chases late payers by hand over chat, and writes receipts on request. It is error-prone and a little awkward socially.
You build the tool the treasurer would use. It is not a payment gateway: residents pay by bank transfer and the treasurer records it. Seed it with fictional flats and residents.
The hard parts are accuracy and tact: a ledger that never drifts, reminders that are correct and polite, receipts that cannot be forged by editing a URL.
must_have: A ledger per flat built from entries (charge, payment, waiver, correction) that are never edited or deleted. Balances are computed from entries, and a correction is a new entry.
Recording a payment (amount, date, mode, bank reference), including partial and advance payments, and refusing the same bank reference twice.
A reminders screen that drafts, for each flat with dues, a message with the right amount and months and a tone tiered by how late it is, ready to copy. The app never sends anything.
A numbered, printable receipt for every payment, sequential within a financial year with no gaps, showing which months it paid.
Treasurer sign-in, and a read-only view where a resident sees only their own flat.
nice_to_have: A month-end summary: collected, outstanding, and aged 30, 60 and 90 days.
Import a bank-statement CSV and propose matches for the treasurer to confirm.
An audit view of who changed what and when.
constraints: No paid services, APIs or accounts. SQLite or a local Postgres is fine.
Fictional data only: made-up flats and residents, example.com addresses and obviously fake phone numbers.
The app never sends a message, e-mail or payment on anyone's behalf.
deliverables: A public repo created after you press Start, with commits spread across the window.
A README with how to run and seed the app, how to run the tests, the sign-in details for the seeded users, and what is missing.
judge_focus: How the ledger stays correct: the model, its invariants, and tests of partial payments, advances and corrections.
Whether a resident can reach only their own flat, and how you checked.
Whether the reminder text is accurate, kind and free of pressure tactics.
A trail of commits: the ledger and its tests first, screens after.
bengaluru_context: Teams building residential-community and property-management products in Bengaluru solve this daily: money owed between neighbours, recorded exactly and asked for politely.
